title.value: A stochastic integer programming approach to reserve staff scheduling with preferences
title.justification: The title clearly reflects the focus of the paper, which is on developing a stochastic integer programming approach for scheduling with preferences, specifically for reserve staff, as indicated in the abstract and throughout the text.
title.quote: A stochastic integer programming approach to reserve staff scheduling with preferences

extractions.description: This paper explores a new approach to scheduling reserve staff with preferences, particularly in the transit industry, using a stochastic integer programming model. The model incorporates employee satisfaction and endogenous uncertainty based on employee preferences and absences, aiming to improve scheduling efficiency and employee welfare.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on optimizing staff scheduling in the transit industry through advanced mathematical programming techniques. While it mentions the transit industry, the paper does not directly address climate or ecologically-related sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We tackle a new variant of the personnel scheduling problem under unknown demand by considering employee satisfaction via endogenous uncertainty depending on the combination of their preferred and received schedules.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not primarily focus on any specific climate or ecologically-related sustainable development category. Although it addresses scheduling in the transit industry, it does not explicitly deal with climate change mitigation or adaptation, natural systems protection, pollution, sustainable finance, or support to developing regions.
primary_category.quote: The goal of the XB days-off scheduling problem is to obtain a work schedule for each XB in the set E of XBs, first consisting of his/her days off and working days for each of the |J| days of the planning horizon.

secondary_categories.justification: Again, while the paper touches on the transit industry, it remains focused on operational and personnel scheduling aspects rather than ecological or sustainable development themes.
secondary_categories.quote: Our contributions summarize as follows. First, we formulate a two-stage stochastic integer program with mixed-integer recourse to model the XB days-off scheduling problem over a finite time horizon.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories listed primarily pertain to direct climate action and sustainability impacts, which are not the focus of this paper. The paper deals with personnel scheduling, which lacks a direct link to any predefined sustainable development sub-category related to climate or ecology.
primary_sub_category.quote: Second, we consider XB preferences in the process to model uncertainty.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Similar to the primary sub-category classification, the paper's content does not align directly with any outlined sustainable development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our approach is validated with an empirical study based on data from the city of Los Angeles.

applications.value: Personnel scheduling optimization in the transit industry
applications.justification: The core application of the paper is optimizing personnel scheduling for reserve staff in the transit industry, addressing employee preferences and handling uncertainties in staffing demands.
applications.quote: We tackle a new variant of the personnel scheduling problem under unknown demand by considering employee satisfaction via endogenous uncertainty.

new_primary_category.justification: No new sustainable development category is suggested since the paper does not introduce novel concepts in ecological or climate sustainability.
new_primary_category.quote: Our work is currently being implemented in a world-leader software solutions provider for public transit operations.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not require a new sub-category as it does not focus on sustainability advancements but rather on scheduling optimization.
